description_full: Envela Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, provides recommerce and recycling services in the United States. It operates in two segments, Consumer and Commercial. The company is involved in the online and brick-and-mortar sale of authenticated high-end luxury goods, including fine jewelry, diamonds and gemstones, luxury watches, and secondary market bullion. It also offers precious metal products. In addition, it provides end-of-life management of IT assets comprising data destruction, asset refurbishment, and remarketing; and detailed asset disposition data services. The company was formerly known as DGSE Companies, Inc. and changed its name to Envela Corporation in December 2019. Envela Corporation was incorporated in 1965 and is headquartered in Irving, Texas.

financial_summary: Envela Corporation is a micro-cap consumer cyclical business with a $280M market cap on $241M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years and +15% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 20% against a 9% cost of capital — a 11-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 19% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $1M in free cash flow — roughly 1 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.18×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
Accruals are elevated at +12.5% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.5× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 45× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 0.1%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 74% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
